description: The Wood Snake in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1965 and 2025 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Snake is the Snake born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the sixth animal. It combines the Snake's insight with Wood's qualities. Wood Snake years between 1924 and 2044 are 1965 and 2025. The Snake's fixed element is Fire.

sections.heading: The Wood Snake personality
paragraphs: The Wood Snake brings growth and generosity to a sign known for insight and poise. The Snake's fixed element is Fire, and Wood generates Fire, so the year stem feeds the animal's inner flame, warming its natural reserve into something more open and creative. Wood Snakes are often described as wise, artistic and thoughtful, with a talent for long-term planning and an appreciation of beauty and learning. They tend to be more sociable and trusting than other Snakes, though still discerning. The nourishing flow gives them steady confidence and a strong intuition. Readings note that Wood Snakes may become attached to comfort, possessions or people, holding on when letting go would be wiser.

Wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak. Classical descriptions link it with kindness, idealism and a talent for cooperation: Wood people are often pictured as the ones who start community projects, mentor younger colleagues and believe that most situations can improve with patience and goodwill. The element also carries a strong sense of fairness and a dislike of waste. Its shadow side, according to most readings, is overextension. Like a plant reaching in every direction, a Wood-year person may take on too much, trust too readily or struggle to say no when a cause seems worthwhile.

sections.heading: Wood Snake at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

Thoughtful, artistic and quietly ambitious, the Wood Snake tends to do its finest work away from the spotlight. Writing, restoration, landscape design, archives and advisory roles are its traditional territory, as depth, patience and aesthetic judgement all pay off there. It needs time to think and a workspace that feels considered. A mentor who trusts its slow-burning projects usually gets remarkable results. In love the Wood Snake is devoted and refined, fond of shared books, gardens and long, unhurried dinners. Loyalty and intellectual intimacy are what it seeks. The difficulty lies in privacy: plans and feelings are kept close, and a partner may sense that the full picture is being withheld.

sections.heading: Wood Snake years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Wood Snake years: 1965, starting Feb 2 and 2025, starting Jan 29. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1965 anyone born before Feb 2 is a Wood Dragon, not a Wood Snake. It takes sixty years for the Wood stem and the Snake branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Wood Snake year is Yin, matching the Snake's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Yi-Si year, the Wood stem Yi with the Snake's branch Si. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Dragon year (before February 2, 1965) and the Wood Dragon year (before January 29, 2025), and births in the weeks after each Wood Snake year ends belong to the Fire Horse. The new year itself fell on a Tuesday in 1965 and Wednesday in 2025.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Snake
paragraphs: Learning to release is usually the Wood Snake's most rewarding work. Clearing clutter, ending stale commitments and loosening attachments to particular outcomes all tend to free their energy. Because they plan carefully, they may also overthink; setting decision dates keeps plans moving. Wood Snakes often benefit from mentoring roles, sharing their accumulated wisdom with others. Creative projects with long horizons, such as writing or garden design, suit their patience. Showing their warmth directly, rather than through subtle gestures, helps others understand them. When generosity and insight work together, the Wood Snake becomes a quietly influential guide.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Snake shares the Snake's San He trine with the Ox and Rooster (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Monkey, and its Liu Chong clash with the Pig. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Snake years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1965 (from February 2, 1965) and 2025 (from January 29, 2025). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Snake's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Snake's fixed element is Fire; in the five-element cycles wood generates Fire. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Snake?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Ox and Rooster (San He) and the Monkey (Liu He). The Pig is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Snake called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Yi-Si. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Yi, followed by its earthly branch, here Si for the Snake, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Snake different from other Snakes?
faq.answer: All Snakes share insight, poise and quiet determination. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
